record.locator: Table 2, row 12 A, p. 17; Results 'Hemilineage 12A', p. 17; Figure 6F,G and legend, p. 18; Figure 3-videos 36, 37
record.quote: Animals expressing CsChrimson in 12 A neurons in one side of the T1 segment showed a single swing movement of the leg
record.other_observation: Figure 6G legend: 'The fly folds both wings outward and swings its right front leg forward upon optogenetic activation.'
record.notes: Coded identically to ADJ-soffers-0001; see that record for the cell reasoning (d13 unclear because the Results attribute wing beating to the undissected animals). DUPLICATE of D0041: same experiment, written by the other curator with a different driver string. Keep one.

reason: Same experiment as D0041 (dissected 12A T1 clones, decapitated, optogenetic). It exists and is a duplicate of D0041; the two did not match only because the driver text differs.

record.driver: TfAP-2-GAL4 with pBPhsFlp2::PEST and 20XUAS>dsFRT>CsChrimson-mVenus (stochastic FLP-based lineage clones; animals not dissected, clones not identified)
record.preparation_detail: headless flies from the same 12A clone experiment that were not dissected, so the clone responsible was not identified
record.effector: 20XUAS>dsFRT>CsChrimson-mVenus, optogenetic activation (red 620-625 nm or halogen white light, 0.2 mM all-trans retinal)
record.coverage_notes: Results: 'We also observed the following behavioral phenotypes in response to optogenetic activation, but we did not dissect the animals to further identify the lineage clone'. Clone extent and location are unknown.
record.quote: high frequency wing beating, backward walking immediately after the stimulus termination, and abdominal extension and bending
record.other_observation: Backward walking occurred immediately after the stimulus ended, not during activation, so it is recorded here and not coded in d8.
